text: Professor Maria Santos of MIT's Department of Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences published a paper in Nature Climate Change showing that Arctic sea ice volume has declined by approximately 13% per decade since satellite measurements began in 1979. The study used a combination of satellite altimetry data and climate model simulations to project that the Arctic could experience its first ice-free summer between 2040 and 2060 under current emission trajectories. Santos noted several sources of uncertainty, including natural variability in ocean circulation patterns and the challenge of accurately modeling cloud feedbacks in polar regions.
